jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE JOB Anduril is seeking a Systems Engineer to support perception system development for the Air Maneuver, Enabling Technology team. The Air Maneuver Team at Anduril develops aerial robotic systems designed to operate in large coordinated teams in concert with ground maneuver forces. Perception is what allows an autonomous aircraft to understand the world immediately around it and act on what it finds there. Delivering that is a sensing problem first. The system spans multiple sensor modalities, the apertures and fields of regard those sensors are installed into, the compute that runs them, and the calibration and timing that turn several sensors into one coherent picture of the world. It is developed once, in ET, and inherited by every MD program that needs it. You will be a key technical leader for that system, and the center of gravity of the role is the sensing suite itself: which sensors are in the baseline and why, what the system is required to detect, at what range, and in what conditions, how that is proven, and what evidence a receiving program gets when the capability transitions onto their aircraft. You will lead this across several concurrent efforts, including in-house sensor development with partner engineering teams elsewhere in Anduril, and new sensing work as the portfolio grows. jobs.description_text: About The Team The Sentry Tower Software team develops robotic systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. About the Job Sentry Towers are robotic systems: motors, cameras, radars, radios, and sensor boards, running on NVIDIA Jetson compute in the field. Verifying that a system like this works means accounting for physical actuation, real sensor data, and hardware that fails in ways no unit test anticipates. We’re hiring a Senior Software Engineer to own our simulation and hardware test infrastructure and make automated, whole-system testing the default for everything we ship. A regression that escapes here does not surface on a developer’s laptop. It surfaces on a tower at a site someone has to fly to, guarding a perimeter that does not pause while we debug. You will work across both halves of the problem. Our software-in-the-loop environments are declaratively defined multi-node virtual towers, complete with a simulated ground control station, synthetic sensor feeds, and a game-engine-driven world, which lets us run whole-system scenarios in CI with no hardware attached. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM Discovery is Anduril's team for the hard concepts: the ones that are not yet proven or built. We take the newest and hardest problems across space, missiles, air, sensors, autonomy, and cyber, decide what is worth building, and prove it out: we build the models, break the assumptions, run the tests, and carry what works to the point where a program can pick it up. We work with hardware and software engineering teams across the company, driving cross-functional collaboration across different business lines. ABOUT THE JOB We are building an expeditionary force: a small group of engineers who want to do big, new, hard things and who move into unfamiliar territory as a matter of course. As a Discovery Engineer you pick up a concept nobody has proven, learn whatever domain it lives in, build the analysis or prototype that tests it, and get to an answer. The problems change; the approach does not: reason from first principles, do the work, check it, and reach a solution. You are not hired for a particular skill set. You are hired for a record of getting engaged in problems across different areas, being analytic, testing new concepts, and getting to solutions. You are also the adversary to our own ideas. The rigor that validates a good concept is the same rigor that kills a bad one early, while it is still cheap, and you apply it to your own work first. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM The Connected Warfare division builds systems to support global command and control missions. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM The Maneuver Dominance team is building Thunder - an autonomous attack rotorcraft built to fight alongside crewed combat aviation to deliver overwhelming mass effects deep beyond the front lines. The team in London builds the Mission System and the autonomy that makes aircraft like Thunder work. Autonomy is only as good as the link that carries it. Thunder is a compact airframe with weapons, sensors and radios competing for the same antenna real estate, flying low and in formation, in a spectrum that is actively contested. That is the problem you are solving. ABOUT THE JOB Anduril is seeking a Senior Systems Engineer to lead the design, integration, verification, and validation of a specific payload or weapon module for the Thunder platform. jobs.title: Senior Systems Engineer, Space Imaging
jobs.department: Mission Systems : Imaging Engineering : Imaging - System Engineering,Integration and Test
jobs.location_raw: Boulder, Colorado, United States · Waltham, Massachusetts, United States
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM The Space Imaging team is seeking a Systems Engineer to join our team. The Imaging Space team is responsible for system architecture definition, trade analyses, and modeling/validating system performance for spaceborne EO/IR systems. In this role, you will be responsible for defining active EO/IR system architectures. You will perform radiometric performance modeling as well as laboratory, ground, and flight testing. To predict real-world performance, you will also model atmospheric and environmental effects for land, sea, and air targets. You will leverage your analyses to inform system-level architectural trades. As needed, you will also lead small teams of engineers from concept ideation through system definition and development. You should have a track record of successfully working on fast-paced, highly technical, interdisciplinary teams. Proficiency in analytical toolchains or languages (e.g., MATLAB, Python) is required. Experience with industry standard EO/IR modeling software packages (e.g. MODTRAN, SPIRITS, AFSIM) is a plus. Prior experience working with space sensors and systems is highly desirable. WHAT YOU’LL DO Define system architectures via detailed trade studies and analyses. Adapt or derive physics-based models of sensor system performance and derive requirements based on those models. jobs.description_text: About the Team The Technology Security and Foreign Disclosure (TSFD) team determines whether Anduril's capabilities can be exported, to whom, and on what authority. We secure the approvals that turn a product into a releasable product: Low Observable and Counter-Low Observable Tri-Service Committee decision memoranda, Critical Program Information assessments, service export baselines, and the disclosure policy that governs what may be said to a partner nation and when. We work across every business line and every service. Our counterparts are SAF/IA, NIPO, DTSA, DASA DE&C, the program executive offices, and the security assistance enterprise. We partner daily with International Trade Compliance on licensing, and with Global Defense capture teams whose pursuits depend on the approvals we obtain. When exportability is the constraint on a campaign, we are the path off it. About the Job This role owns the systems engineering product description and performance review supporting OUSW technology release. You will run the assessment and approval pipeline end to end: scoping product reviews, assembling the artifacts and stakeholders, driving classified assessments to a signed decision, and tracking every open action to closure across dozens of concurrent capabilities and partner nations.
